newsitem.title: UK: STG LOWER IN EUROPE AFTER BOE REPORT, MARK GAINS.
newsitem.headline: STG LOWER IN EUROPE AFTER BOE REPORT, MARK GAINS.

text.p: Sterling was ticking lower against the mark and dollar by the European midsession, pressured by a firmer mark and indications from the Bank of England that a pause in UK monetary policy should now be possible.
Sterling/mark continued its path lower from morning levels, pushing to its lowest levels in over a month after the Bank of England's upbeat report on UK inflation prospects.

The pound took little notice of robust UK employment data and the minutes of the central bank's monetary policy committee's July meeting which indicated a more hawkish stance towards UK interest rates.
"Sterling has been caught in the general mark upmove. The reaction to the data and BOE report has been fairly muted," said Mark Geddes, treasury economist at ABN-Amro in London.
By 1130 GMT, the pound was trading at 2.9054/64 marks, down almost four pfennigs from morning levels and well below late Tuesday's European level of 2.9399/04 marks.
Cable was also weaker but kept to narrower ranges, trading at $1.5750/57 against a morning peak above $1.5840 and short of late Tuesday's $1.5770/80.

Sterling ticked up briefly in earlier trade after news that UK unemployment dropped 49,800 for July and well above a 30,000 drop forecast. This was tempered by static wage inflation for June which stayed at 4.25 percent.
Although today's data did not cause much alarm, analysts said continued falls in jobless numbers could see inflation pressures developing further forward.

Such concerns were raised in the Bank of England MPC July minutes whose members unanimously agreed on July's 25 basis point rate rise. The committee pondered a half-point rise but said this could cause unnecessary sterling strength.
However, the Bank of England's quarterly inflation report painted a more relaxed view on inflation and echoed last week's indications that UK interest rates could remain on hold for the time being.
Although Bank of England deputy governor Mervyn King said today a rate pause need not end with a rate rise, many analysts still see higher UK rates by the end of this year.
"It looks like a pause for another tightening but they will want to see more figures," said Tim Fox, international economist at Standard Chartered Bank in London.
Bank of England's King also said the inflation report projected sterling's trade-weighted index at 90 in two years' time. It was last quoted at 100.9.
Such a fall puts the equivalent sterling/mark level around 2.60, said dealers.
"This is achievable but it's dependent on a lot of other factors that run counter to sterling's current attractiveness, such as yield differentials with Europe," said a UK bank dealer.
The UK central bank's King said they expected a good part of sterling's rise over the last year will unwind over the next two years.
